The rider did delay boarding: the chat shows the rider messaged at 18:24 "Coming down, give me 2 more minutes", and the driver was stationary 41 m from the pickup from 18:22:30 to 18:26:40, so the driver did wait in the rain — the dispute turns only on whether the fee clause conditions were strictly met.

The pre-tap clock: the driver was first within 200 m at 18:21:00 and the platform recorded arrival at 18:21:00, but the "I'm Here" tap came only at 18:22:50, so the NS-1 waiting clock ("waited for > 3 mins for the rider to arrive") is measured from the tap, giving at most 3 min 50 s before the 18:26:40 cancellation — the fee is nonetheless contested because the rider gave notice and was 2 minutes away.

The rider is a 1371-day account holder rated 4.9 with no no-show dispute ever upheld against her (F17), whereas the driver has a no-show dispute already upheld against him within the last 90 days (F18), which supports a rider-favourable exercise of Ryde's discretion over this fee and, at minimum, an account review of the driver's repeated no-show cancellations.

Because the driver cancelled without the rider being able to board, the $6.61 was retained without any trip being provided; under the cancellation-fee rules the fee is refundable to the rider when the NS-1 conditions are not strictly fulfilled, and Ryde's practice is to issue such refunds as a voucher rather than cash.

weaknesses: The strongest fact against the rider is F3/F2/F6: the driver was stationary 41 m from the pickup for 4 min 10 s (F3), within 200 m for a cumulative 5 min 15 s (F2), and tapped "I'm Here" at 18:22:50 with 3 min 50 s of in-range waiting after the tap (F6) — the other side will argue NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are all satisfied and the fee should stand as no_action.

points.response: Conceded on the fact of the tap: F6 records an "I'm Here" press at 18:22:50, 41 m from pickup, but the case files also record F7 that driver_pressed_here_at is null, so NS-1(i)'s first condition is not reliably established and the benefit of that conflict must not be given to the party whose own record is self-contradictory.
The location condition is met on F6/F1 (41 m, and closest approach 38 m at 18:25:25), so I do not contest that the driver was inside the pickup radius at the moment of the tap.

The driver counts 5 min 15 s inside 200 m (F2), but that clock starts at 18:21:00 — before the 18:22:50 arrival tap — and NS-1(iii) counts waiting at the pickup point after the "I'm Here" indication, which is 3 min 50 s at most (F2, F6, F5); the fee's 3-minute threshold is the only measurement the clause provides.

Even on the driver's own arithmetic (arrival tap 18:22:50 to cancellation 18:26:40 = 3 min 50 s, F6, F4), the excess over the 3-minute threshold is only 50 seconds, while the rider had already messaged at 18:24 saying she was coming down and asked for two more minutes (F11); the marginal 50 seconds of a wait in 18.5 mm of rain (F16) is exactly the situation in which Ryde's discretion over the fee should favour the rider.

F11 shows the rider did not dispute the pickup point but was actively on her way and self-limited her delay to two minutes — the message was sent at 18:24 and the driver cancelled at 18:26:40, i.e. 2 min 40 s later, not the "no response" picture the driver's statement (F13) paints, and no system record shows the rider abandoned the trip.

The fee can only stand through NS-1, and because the case files conflict on whether the arrival button was ever pressed (F6 vs F7 = driver_pressed_here_at null), NS-1(i) is not affirmatively proven, so NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full rather than the driver retaining $4.50 (F8).

I do not claim rain waives the fee under NS-2; F16 (heavy rain, 18.5 mm) goes to NS-7 discretion and to the reasonableness of the rider's two-minute request in F11, not to an automatic waiver, and the driver's own no-show history (F18: 1 upheld in 90 days) is the proper target of any pattern argument.

I do not seek an account flag on this ticket for button misuse; my flag argument rests only on profile history (F18, one no-show dispute already upheld in the last 90 days), which under RD-6 may support only an additional review action and never the main finding.

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.85)
events.body:
The fee can only stand through NS-0, which routes a driver-side cancellation asserting rider no-show into NS-1: the driver cancelled at 18:26:40 on a rider-no-show basis [F4][F12][F13][NS-0]. All three NS-1 limbs must therefore hold. Limb (i), the "I'm Here" tap, is established by the timeline record F6 (tap at 18:22:50, 41 m from the pickup) and corroborated by the driver's chat at 18:23 "I'm here at the pickup point" [F6][F10][NS-1]. F7 (driver_pressed_here_at null) is an internal inconsistency in the same record; the corroborated tap at F6 and the driver's own message F10 supply the substantive evidence, so on balance (i) is met [F6][F10][NS-1].

Limb (ii) is not seriously contested: at the moment of the tap the driver was 41 m from the pickup, and his closest approach was 38 m at 18:25:25 [F6][F1][NS-1]. what_would_change: Had the driver tapped I'm Here more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee charged in this case can only stand if the driver satisfies all of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii), i.e. the "I'm Here" tap, GPS presence at the pickup, and more than 3 minutes of waiting there; the record shows the driver in fact tapped "I'm Here" at 18:22:50 while 41 m from the pickup and stayed within 200 m for only 3 min 50 s after that tap.

The rider did delay boarding: the chat shows the rider messaged at 18:24 "Coming down, give me 2 more minutes", and the driver was stationary 41 m from the pickup from 18:22:30 to 18:26:40, so the driver did wait in the rain — the dispute turns only on whether the fee clause conditions were strictly met.

The pre-tap clock: the driver was first within 200 m at 18:21:00 and the platform recorded arrival at 18:21:00, but the "I'm Here" tap came only at 18:22:50, so the NS-1 waiting clock ("waited for > 3 mins for the rider to arrive") is measured from the tap, giving at most 3 min 50 s before the 18:26:40 cancellation — the fee is nonetheless contested because the rider gave notice and was 2 minutes away.

The rider is a 1371-day account holder rated 4.9 with no no-show dispute ever upheld against her (F17), whereas the driver has a no-show dispute already upheld against him within the last 90 days (F18), which supports a rider-favourable exercise of Ryde's discretion over this fee and, at minimum, an account review of the driver's repeated no-show cancellations.

Because the driver cancelled without the rider being able to board, the $6.61 was retained without any trip being provided; under the cancellation-fee rules the fee is refundable to the rider when the NS-1 conditions are not strictly fulfilled, and Ryde's practice is to issue such refunds as a voucher rather than cash.

weaknesses: The strongest fact against the rider is F3/F2/F6: the driver was stationary 41 m from the pickup for 4 min 10 s (F3), within 200 m for a cumulative 5 min 15 s (F2), and tapped "I'm Here" at 18:22:50 with 3 min 50 s of in-range waiting after the tap (F6) — the other side will argue NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are all satisfied and the fee should stand as no_action.

The chat (F11) is the rider's own admission that she was not at the pickup point at 18:24 and needed 2 more minutes, and F12/F13 show the driver called twice with no answer — so the rider's own conduct caused the wait; any relief rests on Ryde's discretion (NS-7), not on a clear failure of the driver.

The weather (F16 heavy rain, 18.5 mm) is a two-way fact: it explains the rider's delay but equally justifies the driver's decision not to wait further, and F14/F15 (band 3 traffic, no incidents) give the driver no fault on the route.

F7 (driver_pressed_here_at is null) conflicts with F6 (tap at 18:22:50); because system records govern and the two timeline entries are inconsistent, the judge may disregard the NS-2 flag_account hook and treat the tap as valid.

Profile facts F17/F18 may not decide the case at all: F17 shows no no-show disputes ever upheld for the rider but also gives nothing that excuses her 2-minute delay, and F18's single upheld no-show dispute is thin support for "repeated" conduct.

claims.assertion: The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 18:22:50 while standing 41 m from the pickup point, so the arrival-button condition is satisfied (GPS confirms 38 m closest approach at 18:25:25 with the vehicle stationary 41 m away).
The driver's position at the moment of the "I'm Here" tap was within the pickup radius: he was 41 m from the pickup point, i.e. inside the 200 m arrival radius.

The driver waited far more than 3 minutes at the pickup point: GPS shows 5 min 15 s cumulative inside 200 m before cancellation, and the timeline shows the vehicle stationary from 18:22:30 to 18:26:40 (4 min 10 s) at 41 m from pickup, so the >180 s waiting condition is met.

The bike was standing at the pickup from 18:22:50 (arrival tap) and cancelled at 18:26:40, i.e. 3 min 50 s of waiting after the arrival indication — above the 3-minute threshold required before a rider no-show cancellation.

The rider herself confirmed in chat at 18:24 that she was still not at the vehicle ("Coming down, give me 2 more minutes"), and the driver additionally called twice before cancelling at 18:26, so the non-appearance is not disputed by the rider's own message.
The $6.61 cancellation fee was correctly applied for a rider no-show and should stand, of which $4.50 is payable to the driver.

The heavy rain (18.5 mm) is not a reason to waive the fee: Ryde's cancellation framework conditions the fee only on arrival, position and waiting time, all of which the driver satisfied; the app records no driver-side ground for waiver.
Because the driver met every NS-1 condition, this is not a case of misuse of the cancellation/waiting button, so no account flag against the driver is warranted on this ticket.

weaknesses: The fact table contains two conflicting timeline entries about the arrival button: F6 states the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 18:22:50, 41 m from pickup, while F7 states the driver never tapped it (driver_pressed_here_at is null). If the judge adopts F7, NS-1(i) fails and the $6.61 must be refunded in full under NS-2, so the rider will press F7 against us.

The rider will argue her 18:24 message (F11) was an accepted request for more time and that she only asked for two extra minutes, which she will say was reasonable in heavy rain (F16); the driver cancelled 2 min 40 s after that message.
The driver's own 90-day history includes 1 upheld no-show dispute (F18), which the rider may use to argue a pattern, although the profile alone cannot decide this case under the policy.

There is no traffic evidence to justify any driver-side excuse for speed or delay: F15 shows no incidents and F14 shows only band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Maxwell Road, so the driver cannot rely on RD-4 style congestion evidence for anything.

points.response: Conceded on the fact of the tap: F6 records an "I'm Here" press at 18:22:50, 41 m from pickup, but the case files also record F7 that driver_pressed_here_at is null, so NS-1(i)'s first condition is not reliably established and the benefit of that conflict must not be given to the party whose own record is self-contradictory.
The location condition is met on F6/F1 (41 m, and closest approach 38 m at 18:25:25), so I do not contest that the driver was inside the pickup radius at the moment of the tap.

The driver counts 5 min 15 s inside 200 m (F2), but that clock starts at 18:21:00 — before the 18:22:50 arrival tap — and NS-1(iii) counts waiting at the pickup point after the "I'm Here" indication, which is 3 min 50 s at most (F2, F6, F5); the fee's 3-minute threshold is the only measurement the clause provides.

Even on the driver's own arithmetic (arrival tap 18:22:50 to cancellation 18:26:40 = 3 min 50 s, F6, F4), the excess over the 3-minute threshold is only 50 seconds, while the rider had already messaged at 18:24 saying she was coming down and asked for two more minutes (F11); the marginal 50 seconds of a wait in 18.5 mm of rain (F16) is exactly the situation in which Ryde's discretion over the fee should favour the rider.

F11 shows the rider did not dispute the pickup point but was actively on her way and self-limited her delay to two minutes — the message was sent at 18:24 and the driver cancelled at 18:26:40, i.e. 2 min 40 s later, not the "no response" picture the driver's statement (F13) paints, and no system record shows the rider abandoned the trip.

The fee can only stand through NS-1, and because the case files conflict on whether the arrival button was ever pressed (F6 vs F7 = driver_pressed_here_at null), NS-1(i) is not affirmatively proven, so NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full rather than the driver retaining $4.50 (F8).

I do not claim rain waives the fee under NS-2; F16 (heavy rain, 18.5 mm) goes to NS-7 discretion and to the reasonableness of the rider's two-minute request in F11, not to an automatic waiver, and the driver's own no-show history (F18: 1 upheld in 90 days) is the proper target of any pattern argument.

I do not seek an account flag on this ticket for button misuse; my flag argument rests only on profile history (F18, one no-show dispute already upheld in the last 90 days), which under RD-6 may support only an additional review action and never the main finding.

The rider's own framing defeats her: the record she cites shows the tap at 18:22:50 (F6), and the 3 min 50 s of in-range waiting after that tap is above the 3-minute threshold NS-1 requires, while the cumulative in-range time was 5 min 15 s (F2) — all three NS-1 conditions are met, so the fee stands.

Conceded as far as it goes: the rider admits at 18:24 she was not at the vehicle (F11) and the driver waited stationary 41 m away for 4 min 10 s (F3); the rider shows no failure of any NS-1 condition, only that she was late.

Measuring the clock from the tap is exactly what NS-1 requires, and it yields 3 min 50 s of waiting before the 18:26:40 cancellation (F6, F4) — above the "more than 3 minutes" threshold; the rider's notice that she needed "2 more minutes" at 18:24 (F11) expired well before the driver cancelled, and a request for time does not suspend the rider's obligation to appear.

Profile facts cannot decide a case — F17 and F18 may support a flag_account request at most, and here the driver's single upheld no-show dispute in 90 days against 317 trips (F18) does not meet the "repeated" standard, so no account action and no fee waiver follow from them.

The refund route in NS-2 only opens when NS-1 is not satisfied; since all three NS-1 conditions are satisfied (F6, F2, F3), that route is closed, and the $6.61 already charged on the record (F8) is correctly retained, with $4.50 due to the driver.
